newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney proceeds with development.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney proceeds with development.

text.p: Theme park operator Euro Disney said adjacent development projects were proceeding and it expected government approvals for the development of the urban centre of Val d'Europe to be concluded by May.

"Euro Disney SCA is continuing its development, with many new projects that will not only add exciting features to the Disneyland Paris resort but will also serve as a catalyst for the development of the urban centre of Val d'Europe," it said in its 1995/96 earnings statement.
"Most of this development will be financed by third parties."
The opening in July of a Planet Hollywood restaurant marked the expansion of the Disney Village, formerly called the Festival Disney entertainment centre.
An eight-screen Gaumont cinema under construction is expected to open in March.

"Other innovative projects are being negotiated with French and international brand names in the leisure and restaurant sectors to further strengthen the group's entertainment offering and...pave the way for additional restaurants and retail shops," it said.

A second convention centre under construction next to Disney Village is expected to open in the autumn of 1997 and will double the group's convention capacity. The financing has been provided by The Walt Disney Co, which owns 39 percent of Euro Disney, in the form of a leasing agreement.

"The group has officially notified the public authorities of its intention to launch the development of the urban centre of Val d'Europe. Various government approvals are expected to be finalised by May 1997. This project includes the construction of retail space combining a traditional shopping centre and an upscale factory outlet village called Pavillon de la Mode," Euro Disney said.

"Commercial real estate master development on the site is also well under way. A first phase around the town of Bailly-Romainvilliers is now completed. The next phase will involve housing within and around the golf course as well as in the urban centre of Val d'Europe," it said.
Euro Disney has previously said that, further down the line, it plans to build a second theme park.
